samuel1.17.p1.b1.text: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war … Saul and the men of Israel assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, arraying themselves for battle …

samuel1.17.p1.b2.text: The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.

samuel1.17.p2.b3.text: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height …

samuel1.17.p2.b4.text: … a bronze helmet on his head. He wore a bronze coat of mail … armor of bronze on his legs and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.

samuel1.17.p2.b5.text: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. In addition, his shield bearer went before him.

samuel1.17.p3.b6.text: Why do you come out and array yourselves for battle? … Choose one of your men and have him come down against me.

samuel1.17.p3.b7.text: I defy the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man to fight!

samuel1.17.p3.b8.text: On hearing the words of the Philistine, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.

samuel1.17.p4.b9.text: And David was the youngest. The three oldest had followed Saul, but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.

samuel1.17.p4.b10.text: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand.

samuel1.17.p4.b11.text: Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.

samuel1.17.p5.b12.text: So David got up early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out …

samuel1.17.p5.b13.text: … the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came forward from the Philistines and shouted his usual words, which David also heard.

samuel1.17.p5.b14.text: When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear.

samuel1.17.p6.b15.text: To the man who kills him the king will give great riches. And he will give him his daughter in marriage …

samuel1.17.p6.b16.text: Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

samuel1.17.p6.b17.text: Why have you come down here? … I know your pride and wickedness of heart—you have come down to see the battle!

samuel1.17.p6.b18.text: What have I done now? … Was it not just a question?

samuel1.17.p7.b19.text: Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!

samuel1.17.p7.b20.text: You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.

samuel1.17.p7.b21.text: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.

samuel1.17.p7.b22.text: Go … and may the LORD be with you.

samuel1.17.p8.b23.text: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.

samuel1.17.p8.b24.text: I cannot walk in these … I am not accustomed to them.

samuel1.17.p8.b25.text: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.

samuel1.17.p9.b26.text: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.

samuel1.17.p9.b27.text: Am I a dog … that you come at me with sticks?

samuel1.17.p9.b28.text: You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts …

samuel1.17.p9.b29.text: … for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands.

samuel1.17.p10.b30.text: As the Philistine started forward to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.

samuel1.17.p10.b31.text: Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead.

samuel1.17.p10.b32.text: The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.

samuel1.17.p11.b33.text: Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand …

samuel1.17.p11.b34.text: David ran and stood over him. He grabbed the Philistine’s sword and pulled it from its sheath …

samuel1.17.p11.b35.text: When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran. Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines …

samuel1.17.p12.b36.text: Abner, whose son is this young man?

samuel1.17.p12.b37.text: As surely as you live, O king … I do not know.

samuel1.17.p12.b38.text: Whose son are you, young man?

samuel1.17.p12.b39.text: I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem
